newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dlr ends firmer as exporters sell U.S. unit.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dlr ends firmer as exporters sell U.S. unit.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed slightly higher against its American counterpart on Saturday on active U.S. dollar sales by exporters, dealers said.
The local dollar ended at T$27.386 against Friday's T$27.391 close. Turnover through dealers was US$115 million.
Dealers said the Taiwan dollar opened lower in reaction to the strength of the U.S. dollar overseas.
"But then exporters started to sell U.S. dollars as they saw current levels as a good chance to sell, reversing the trend," said one dealer.
The Taiwan dollar's recent sharp appreciation has almost come to end and it should enter a more stable period, dealers said.
"Anticipation for a Taiwan dollar uptrend has eased, and it should be stable in the near term," said one.
A T$27.35-27.45 range was seen for the week ahead.
